newsitem.title: USA: WHX begins tender offer for Dynamics Corp.
newsitem.headline: WHX begins tender offer for Dynamics Corp.

text.p: WHX Corp. said Monday it began a cash tender offer for the stock of Dynamics Corp. of America at $40 apiece to increase its stake in the appliance and equipment manufacturer to 19.9 percent.
"Today was the first step," said Richard Aldrick, an analyst at Lehman Brothers. "Now, WHX is going to slowly try to take control of the company."
WHX, which already owns 109,600 Dynamics shares, said its tender offer is for up to 649,000 shares.
The stake is the biggest WHX could acquire without triggering Dynamics' "poison pill" anti-takeover measure, which kicks in when one party acquires more than 20 percent of Dynamics' stock.
WHX, the holding company for steelmaker Wheeling, Pittsburgh Steel Corp., said it would buy fewer shares if Dynamics lowers the "poison pill" trigger to below 20 percent.
Dynamics responded that the "unanimous initial reaction" of its directors to the offer, except for one who could not be reached, was that it was "totally inadequate."

WHX said that late last week it sent a letter to Dynamics proposing a cash merger at $40 per share, or a total of about $160 million. WHX said it was prepared to raise its offer if Dynamics could prove that it was worth more.
In a statement, Dynamics said it acknowledged receipt of WHX's unsolicited offer on Thursday, and advised WHX it would inform its directors and respond this week.
Dynamics said it was suggesting that its shareholders withhold taking any action on the offer pending further developments.
Dynamics' stock jumped $5, or more than 15 percent, to $38.125, while WHX fell 25 cents to $6.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The offer expires on April 29, it said.

WHX said that once it owns 19.9 percent of Dynamics, it would adopt new shareholder by-laws permitting owners of more than a 9.9 percent stake to call special company meetings. It also said it would name new members to Dynamics' board.
WHX said the offer is not subject to any minimum number of shares being tendered or to financing. As of Dec. 31, it said it had more than $400 million of available cash and cash equivalents.
With that kind of cash stockpile, the acquisition came as no surprise to some analysts. Others, however, said the companies have widely different businesses and that WHX's strategy seemed unclear.

Dynamics, based in Greenwich, Conn., makes a variety of electrical appliances and electronic devices, fabricated metal products and equipment, and power and controlled environmental systems. It holds a 44.1 percent stake in CTS Corp. which makes electronic and electromechanical components.

"My initial reaction is there's probably not much by way of synergies for these two companies, but the acquisition would be a diversification away from steel into more value-added products for WHX," said Lehman's Aldrich.
WHX said its tender offer for the Dynamics shares ends April 29.
